newsitem.title: USA: DC Metro rail no fare increase for 18 months - paper.
newsitem.headline: DC Metro rail no fare increase for 18 months - paper.

text.p: Metro rail and bus riders would see no fare increases or service cuts for at least 18 months, but some local governments, including the District, would have to contribute more money to the region's transit system under a spending plan proposed by the agency on Thursday, the Washington Post reported on Friday.

The $637.8 million proposal for the fiscal year beginning July 1 would help finance several improvements to the Metro's subway system, including the extension of the blue line to a new Franconia/Springfield station and two new station entrance openings, the paper reported.
The plan also calls for 32 more security personnel.
District of Columbia representatives criticized the plan's call for a $2 million increase of the already cash-strapped District's transit contribution.
If the District cannot afford a subsidy increase, transit officials say they could be forced to either cut Metro's budget or raise fares and cut services in the District, the paper reported.
Metro's budget committee has scheduled a series of meetings on the budget, which will be approved in April and sent to the eight localities srved by Metro.
